headline: Highest risk is data leakage: ChatGPT Desktop can read user files/screens/clipboard while awesome-selfhosted is a static docs-only list, creating a default path for sensitive content to leave the local workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a static open-source knowledge-management list with no runtime I/O, so it cannot inject ChatGPT Desktop directly. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or file-based transfer into ChatGPT Desktop’s clipboard/files surfaces, which makes prompt injection possible but unusual and limited to what the operator pastes.
conditions: IF the operator copies content from awesome-selfhosted into ChatGPT Desktop prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used to interpret pasted repository text as instructions, malicious text can steer outputs.
mitigations: Paste only short excerpts, not whole pages.
Strip markdown/code blocks before sending to ChatGPT Desktop.
Use a separate review prompt that treats pasted text as untrusted data.
Manually verify any instruction-like text before acting on it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, clipboard, and files from supported macOS apps, while awesome-selfhosted is a docs-only repository/list that may be copied into those surfaces. That creates a default leakage path for any sensitive material the operator places alongside the list, even though awesome-selfhosted itself does not generate secrets.
conditions: IF the operator pastes or uploads sensitive notes together with awesome-selfhosted content, ChatGPT Desktop can ingest them.
IF files from supported macOS apps contain sensitive data and are opened in ChatGPT Desktop, that data may flow to the vendor backend.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace.
Use a dedicated non-sensitive browser/profile for the list.
Disable clipboard sharing during review sessions.
Redact secrets before uploading any file or screenshot.
Review only public repository content in ChatGPT Desktop.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. ChatGPT Desktop can read files and use clipboard/screen capture, but it cannot write the filesystem or modify git state here. The pair therefore has no meaningful write-write conflict beyond manual operator actions.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies outputs into a shared git working tree, human-mediated conflicts can occur.
IF another tool is added that grants write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep ChatGPT Desktop read-only for this workflow.
Avoid editing the same files in parallel.
Use git status before and after any manual paste.
Separate review and edit sessions.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can treat pasted or screen-captured content as input and then produce downstream advice, so if awesome-selfhosted entries are summarized into ChatGPT prompts, errors can cascade from the list into generated recommendations. The list itself is not authoritative, but the pair still supports an A-to-B handoff without built-in verification.
conditions: IF the operator asks ChatGPT Desktop to act on summaries copied from awesome-selfhosted, downstream recommendations may inherit errors.
IF ChatGPT Desktop output is used without independent verification, mistaken tool choices can propagate.
mitigations: Require a second source before acting on any recommendation.
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to quote the exact source line used.
Compare outputs against the original repository entry.
Mark all copied content as untrusted input.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class is identified in awesome-selfhosted, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch to cite for it. ChatGPT Desktop does handle uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and app content, which can create compliance exposure if the operator places regulated data into the pair, but the profile does not prove such data is present.
conditions: IF regulated data is pasted, uploaded, or screen-captured into ChatGPT Desktop, compliance obligations may apply.
IF the operator uses the pair for data subject or retention-sensitive material, policy mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Do not use regulated data in this workflow.
Confirm the data class before uploading anything.
Use a local-only review path for sensitive material.
Delete temporary files after the session.
Consult the vendor docs before processing regulated content.
